306410.subject: Physics
306410.text: The specific heat capacity of a body is dependent upon
306410.sol: Specific heat capacity is defined as the amount of heat required to raise the temperature of unit mass of a substance by one degree. It is an intrinsic property of the substance. Therefore, it depends only on the nature of the material of the body and is independent of its mass, the heat supplied, or the rise in temperature.
